A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DSeq-JEPA. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, and figures, support comparison despite substantial rewriting and reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original DSeq-JEPA classification, detection, segmentation, and CLEVR experiments, alongside component ablations, visualization analyses, and training-time measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds ImageNet fine-tuning, ViT-H evaluations, attention-proxy and truncation ablations, and additional computational measurements.

M1.justification: The default saliency-guided region selection, probabilistic curriculum, sequential prediction, and Huber objective remain. v2 introduces a label-free Grad-CAM replacement for the saliency stage specifically as an ablation variant (Table 7 and Appendix A.1). DSeq-C-JEPA is the renamed existing DSeq-JEPA+Contrastive variant, not a new core method.

E1.justification: Both versions use ImageNet-1K, iNaturalist21, CUB, Stanford Cars, MS-COCO, ADE20K, and CLEVR Count/Distance for the same task families. Added fine-tuning, larger backbones, and ablations change experimental settings rather than dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v1's benchmark comparisons largely comprise I-JEPA and C-JEPA. v2 Table 1 adds reported comparisons with MAE, DINO, iBOT, LeJEPA, and NEPA; Table 2 adds MAE, DINO, iBOT, and NEPA to dense prediction. The CLEVR comparator set remains unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds ImageNet full fine-tuning with a 50-epoch AdamW protocol and batch size 512, plus ViT-H/16 pre-training for 300 epochs at 448×448, beyond the retained 600-epoch, 224×224 ViT-B/L settings. New diagnostic settings include Top-3 truncation and an alternative attention proxy. Table 1 also includes fine-tuning accuracy in its average, changing the aggregation from four evaluation columns to five.

E4.justification: v2 adds focused tests of prediction-chain truncation and attention-proxy robustness (Tables 5 and 7), and extends the existing timing analysis to memory, compute, and inference costs (Table 8). Spatial/random ordering, region-count sensitivity, and per-step difficulty were already evaluated in v1's appendix. The random-order iNat21 result and two training-clustering examples are removed.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or actual significance tests. The per-step prediction-loss analysis continues to average over 10,000 ImageNet images; no new uncertainty-estimation practice is introduced.

E6.justification: Matched ViT-B/L linear-probing, dense-prediction, and CLEVR scores are retained. Substantial new entries include DSeq-JEPA ImageNet fine-tuning accuracies of 84.0/86.8 for ViT-B/L, ViT-H linear/fine-tuning results of 82.4/87.8, truncation accuracy 73.0, Grad-CAM accuracy 73.4, and expanded baseline/resource results. Separate literature-reported I-JEPA/C-JEPA rows and the random-order iNat21 score of 35.0 disappear. Changed Table 1 averages reflect the added fine-tuning column, not improvements under the old aggregation.

T1.justification: v2 Equation (6) corrects v1 Equation (5) from a sum and normalization over N steps to N−1, avoiding an out-of-range next-region target and matching the prediction range already described in v1. Appendix A.1 also defines the new ablation's gradient-based saliency proxy. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that discriminative region prioritization and sequential latent prediction jointly improve transferable, fine-grained representations across the same task families. v2's explicit contribution list and expanded supporting experiments do not materially redefine this central contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations that later, lower-saliency regions provide complementary supervision and that meaningful ordering matters more than the particular attention proxy. It clarifies that added computational costs occur during pre-training and acknowledges unmatched NEPA configurations. v1's information-maximization explanation, causal-dependency wording, and unsupported statistical-significance assertion are removed or softened.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1 adds ViT-H settings, ImageNet fine-tuning instructions, and the Grad-CAM implementation; Table 8 expands resource reporting. Conversely, v1's component threshold α=0.15, max-pooling window of 3, explicit CLEVR VTAB-1k split sizes, and official-code/reimplementation/published-result annotations disappear. Most optimization and downstream details and the project link remain. These omissions do not establish changes to the underlying experiments.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning against autoregressive visual learning and contemporary predictive methods, discussing RandSAC, LeJEPA, and NEPA and explicitly distinguishing discriminatively ordered latent prediction from iGPT-style reconstruction. DINO, iBOT, and Grad-CAM references are added. Several human-perception, BERT/GPT, and transformer-memory references supporting v1's framing are removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, methodology, and results discussion are extensively rewritten. v2 adds explicit contribution bullets, reorganizes the method around two components, moves architecture details into Appendix A.1, and integrates several former appendix analyses into the main text. Terminology, the contrastive variant's name, and the author list also change.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout. Figure 1 is replaced and Figures 2–3 are substantially redrawn; the former appendix loss curve becomes a main-text bar chart. Benchmark and efficiency tables gain columns and rows, the CLEVR table is transposed, and clustering panels are reduced or rearranged. These are extensive visual changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: v2 improves the paper's evidentiary context through broader comparisons, fine-tuning and scaling evaluations, targeted mechanism checks, and fuller efficiency reporting. The rewritten organization and corrected loss expression also improve clarity. These benefits are tempered by removal of baseline provenance and reproducibility details, while some new comparisons use unmatched configurations and cannot establish controlled superiority. The net improvement is supported but limited in rigor.
